You are a blind semantic decoder of natural-language crystal descriptions. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Read its spatial meaning, identify the coordinate convention and symmetry, resolve numerical relations, and produce a finite crystal construction plan. Do not assume unstated positional values, look up a named material, or claim a complete reconstruction when required information is missing.
Return one JSON object only, without a Markdown fence. For a complete conventional-cell description use this schema:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"literal Hall symbol specified in the prose","lattice":[a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma],"composition":{"Element":integer_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[fractional_x,fractional_y,fractional_z]}]}
Lengths are in angstroms and angles in degrees. Copy the Hall symbol from the description, preserving its mathematical meaning; the geometry engine resolves the public-table integer index, so do not guess a Hall number. Each representative may be any equivalent point of that Wyckoff orbit in the declared Hall setting. List each independent orbit once; multiple orbits of the same element remain separate. The geometry engine will apply all public Hall-setting symmetry operations, retain unique points per orbit, and write the full unit cell. Sites have full occupancy in this pilot.
Use the supplied meanings and numbers rather than matching any fixed wording. You may rely on public crystallographic definitions to identify a Wyckoff orbit or Hall convention. If the text does not determine the necessary lattice, independent positions or setting, return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for incompatible constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Do not output guessed coordinates to fill missing information.

The structure crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Pnma (No. 62), with the Hall symbol -P 2ac 2n, and possesses a primitive lattice defined by the parameters a = 7.11 Å, b = 5.33 Å, and c = 9.75 Å, with all interaxial angles constrained to 90°. The unit cell contains a total of twelve atoms, comprising eight terbium and four magnesium atoms, which are distributed across three independent crystallographic orbits. All atoms reside on the mirror planes perpendicular to the b-axis, specifically occupying the Wyckoff 4c positions with the coordinate relation (x, 1/4, z), where the y-coordinate is fixed at one-quarter.

The terbium sublattice is split into two inequivalent 4c orbits. The first terbium orbit is defined by the independent parameters x = 0.318 and z = 0.416, while the second terbium orbit is characterized by x = 0.467 and z = 0.728. The magnesium atoms occupy a single 4c orbit with independent parameters x = 0.247 and z = 0.124. All three orbits have a multiplicity of four and an occupancy of unity, with the representative atoms situated on the y = 1/4 plane.

The atomic arrangement is organized into two distinct planes stacked along the b-axis. The first plane is located at a fractional coordinate of y = 0.25 and contains four terbium atoms and two magnesium atoms. The second plane, related by the symmetry operations of the space group, is positioned at y = 0.75 and contains an identical distribution of four terbium and two magnesium atoms. This layering results in a three-dimensional framework where the atomic positions are fully described by the specified fractional coordinates along the a, b, and c axes, with the standard Hall frame and original input frame being identical.
